answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before accessing valuable work. Completed jobs add signed results and dispute outcomes to its thread; verifiers check them against an on-chain anchor before raising its limits. A new identity has no history, and copying another agent’s record does not copy its signatures or stake. To create a swarm, an attacker must fund each deposit and risk losing collateral when fraud is proven. A shale-thin reputation earns little trust.
